utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become IC 383.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Lieutenant van der Weijden, can you tell us the steps that a shooter would take to compensate for all of these factors that affect the trajectory of the bullet?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: For this -- the shooter has the ability of his -- the distance measuring methods, so nowadays use -- well mostly it is done by laser range finding. Before he would use his calculation, the map or as I explained before, he would compensate for that in -- with the use of a table which tells him at what distance, how many adjustments he has to make to the sight to compensate for the influences, so for the wind or the distance or upward angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, you told us earlier this afternoon about shooting from a static location. Do you remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In terms of compensating for these various factors, would there be certain advantages for a shooter who was at a static location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There would be. If you arrive at a -- during an offensive operation, you end up -- you arrive at a location, you usually only have one moment for the shot, so you would have to be very secure, if you are in a static position for a longer time, you would be able to take shots, see what their impact is, and compensate for the impact so that next time when shooting on that location, on the exact same spot, you would be able to hit the spot where you intend to hit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're going to turn now, Lieutenant, to the specific incidents, the 12 incidents that are contained in your report. And before we do that, I'd like you to again just very briefly tell us, we will turn first to incident number 1, which is page 9 in the written report, page 10 in e-court, and again it's P 09808 and in e-court page 10, otherwise page 9 of the hard copy. Now, Lieutenant, again, to be as general as possible, can you tell us using this incident as an example, the steps that you took while on the mission in Mostar in the autumn of 2004?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this would be a good moment so that I only have to do this once, but for the record I would like to place on the record my objection to the witness being asked for his opinion on these incidents. Now, this has been a very interesting symposium on various aspects of shooting and, like everybody else in the courtroom, I admire the work that Your Honours have done in preparation for this and your knowledge of these aspects. But this is a trial. And we have to have some standards here. What's going on is this: That a decade after the event this witness, who has no background in criminal investigation whatsoever, is going to be asked to reconstruct these events. Your Honour, if I may finish, we've had a long afternoon, I'm only asking for two minutes here. There is a class of expert witnesses called ballistics experts whose job is to reconstruct crime scenes. This witness is not such an expert. No contemporary investigation was done. He has not spoken to any of the witnesses. It's speculation on speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Murphy, the Chamber has decided that this witness should testify. So this does not pose a problem of any kind for us. In our opinion he is quite capable of testifying. The Prosecution is now showing him a sketch that he drafted and the Prosecution will ask him why he drafted such a sketch, why he determined that there were certain angles there. We will draw our conclusions and in the course of your cross-examination you can prove the contrary. You will have ample opportunity to demonstrate that his work is of no worth. But before that, we want to listen to the witness. We are -- you are making us waste time. We are not a common law system, we are working within a system of international justice, and there is a procedure that provides for expert witnesses to testify. And the Judges decide on matters after the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination has been conducted. We have to establish beyond all reasonable doubt where the shots were fired from. We had a witness who came here to explain these things to us. We now have someone who has come to provide with other information. Mr. Praljak provided us with demonstration to the contrary. You may also act in that manner. So there we have it. Mr. Mundis please continue, and, Mr. Murphy, if you want to repeat that, you will do so in the course of your cross-examination. The transcript says that it's not an expert witness and [indiscernible] would be best for him to leave immediately. We have understood your submission, but we believe that the examination should continue. So please continue, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Lieutenant van der Weijden could you please use incident one as an example to give us more detail of how you went about producing the report in -- of the incidents in terms of what you did while in Mostar in the autumn of 2004, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Using incident one, the first three captions, the situation, GPS reading, and alleged shooting position, those were the -- was the information provided to me in the summary. I visited the incident site at the exact GPS reading, with the use of a GPS at the location of the victim. I set up a tripod with a laser range finder and scanned the -- the surroundings for possible shooting locations, taking into account the type wound that was caused, made a sketch of the situation to include in the report, and determine the range to the location which I thought was most suitable as a shooting location. I included additional information from the distance at the time I -- together with the investigator, I -- I also made a stop with a good overview of Mostar at which -- with the naked eye, as well as with the use of optics tried to distinguish at the larger distances if I would be able to identify people as combatant or non-combatant, so if they would be female, elderly people. And that's included into the -- the report. Additionally, I visited the alleged shooting location to get an image, if it would be able, if it would make a good shooting position. Because not always is the alleged shooting position suitable for the -- for the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And with respect to incident number 1, when you talk about the alleged shooting position, where did you actually go?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I went to Stotina, which was on the map of -- would point out with one of the maps that I -- can I use this on -- yeah? On the map of Mostar that the house is visible, and I circled the house here, that is the house in front of which I took the photos. I took the photo on the second page of the incident description two metres in front of the house, towards the incident sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask, I have a still photo and I would ask that that be shown to the witness. Sir, do you recognise what's visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, these are -- this is the house, the house that I encircled is the house from which I believe the shots were fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let me be very precise in my question, sir. At the time you visited this location and you have told us about taking the photograph, can you place an X on the approximate location where you were stand when you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Lieutenant van der Weijden, while you were at this location in Stotina, did you at any point in time go into the house that you have circled?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not, that was not possible at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for us approximately, and I can see from the X, but can you describe for us approximately how far away from the house you were at the time you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would be two metres in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let's perhaps if you could again sign this photograph, we would ask for an IC number with respect to that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will become Exhibit IC 384.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now if we could please turn in the hard copy to page 10 of your report, and this in e-court would be page 11 of P 09808. The photograph that you see on this page, can you tell us, sir, how this picture was produced?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This picture was produced with the use of a digital camera, which did have zoom but which I don't use because I took the photo through the lens of the laser range finder which has a seven times magnification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you compare this photograph, sir, with what would be visible to an individual with a scope on a rifle?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This would be very similar, and you can see in the picture the sort of a reticle which is an example of the reticles used in most optics which aid in the judging of distance in case the laser fails. And it's similar to what a shooter would see through a scope. It is taken through a seven times magnification, but the compression of the photo would reduce it to somewhat -- six times magnification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, in producing your report or this photograph in particular, can you tell us about the arrow that's been placed on the photograph? Who put that there and what that represents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I placed the arrow with the letters beneath of case number 1. I placed them on the -- on the photo myself, and to precisely point out the location of the victim at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Lieutenant van der Weijden, because you were standing two metres in front of the house at Stotina, what would be the effect on this view if you would have been inside the house?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There would be no effect apart from if I could see the -- the picture of the house again. Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record I believe this is IC 384 that we are returning to.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: As is visible on the house, there are four windows there. At the time that I visited the house, or the -- Mostar, all windows were breaked up, so there was no window anymore. And the lower levels didn't have any windows, but were blocked from view from this incident site by the rocks in front of the house. For that I determined that the higher levels would be very suitable as a location from which the shots came from, but the higher angle would only me -- give more sight on the location by going up into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, based on the steps that you took while visiting both the Stotina location and the location of the shooting, can you tell us the distance between those two locations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The distance was taken with the laser range finder and was 760 metres, which includes the -- the deviation of plus two or minus two metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Lieutenant van der Weijden, in light of the specific instructions that you were given in producing this report, and which you have told us about, can you tell us what your conclusions were with respect to this incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The conclusions were -- if we would look at page 9, the sketch in combination with the photo on page 10, there was -- there were too many structures on -- behind the victim or on the eastern side of Mostar, I believe. Which would rule out the -- the possibility of the shooter being at that location. The problems on the other side of the river, well the victim indicates that he was shot at a -- when -- in the standing in a certain position, from that I concluded that the shot came more or less from down the river, so down the river of Neretva instead of the opposite side of the river which led me to conclude that looking in that direction the only good option there was for the shooter would be the houses at Stotina or the house at Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for the record, when you say the house in Stotina, which house are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's the one that I have encircled on the picture. This one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's -- -- let's turn please to incident 2, which is -- or pages 11 and 12 of the hard copy. Pages 12 and 13 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you can intervene tomorrow. We have to finish. So tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will lose 10 minutes coming back to this tomorrow, so may we go back to the first case and could the Prosecutor ask the witness on the photograph where the victim was exactly when he was hit? There is a number 30, and an arrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you will have ample time to ask in the cross-examination. Continue, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn to incident 2. You've already told us how the steps you took with respect to incident one. Were those steps the same for incident two in terms of what you did to produce this part of your report, or did you do anything differently?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The difference in this case was because of the picture on page 12, in that picture I highlighted a building that I learned from the investigator at the time, which was checked through the cadastre that that house was built after the incident, time of incident, which now blocks the view on the -- on the incident from Stotina. This picture was also taken from the same location as incident number one. It did mean that I took two steps back, a couple of steps back to get a clear view of the house, to determine the direction of fire, because along the street there was no other suitable location for the shooter to be at, apart from standing out in the open on the street. So that's the difference. In this incident, I stepped back, and the difference as well is that in the situation a fragmentation bullet is mentioned, in my opinion fragmentation bullets don't -- they are not -- it would be technically possible to make a bullet that would strike -- that would disintegrate on striking on the -- when striking the target, but in my opinion and experience, when shooting through glass, which was the case in this, a bullet is stripped of its copper -- copper coating, which -- and -- if the bullet would have been consisted of the steel tip with a lead core that would already mean that there were three separate parts of the bullet within -- just after the windshield, which would cause wounds similar to fragmentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I misunderstood part of your answer, sir, during the course of that answer, but at -- can you tell us again for the record with respect to an -- I'm focusing now on the photograph on page 12 or page 13 in e-court. Can you tell us, if you were standing at the location where the victim was or at another location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The location from which I took the picture was taken from two metres in front of the house in Stotina. And the arrow indicates the location of the victim, which is -- was just below the roof line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And again, sir, can you tell us based on the steps that you took while on mission the distance between the alleged location in Stotina, or the house in Stotina, and the spot where the victim was located when shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Because of the new building blocking the view, what I did is I marked that spot where the victim was shot, took enough distance back to get a clear view of Stotina, and then measured the distance from the location where I took -- lasered the distance to the distance of the victim and added that to the total distance. And then I came to a 426 metres in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, in light of the instructions that you were provided and which you have told us about earlier today, what conclusions did you draw with respect to incident number 2?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Incident number 2, also because of the buildings visible on the -- on the sketch, and the -- the bullet striking the front windshield of the truck, the -- I concluded that the bullet must have come from the general direction of Stotina in which -- in looking in that direction the best option for a shooter location would be the house in Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, when you say the house in Stotina, which house are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would be the same house as this one. The other ones were not visible from the incident site because they were blocked by the rocks, but the upper levels of the encircled house were visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that's the how that you have circled on the IC -- is it 386?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Or 384, IC 384. Thank you. Can we turn now, please, to incident number 3, which is described in pages 13 and 14 of your report, in e-court pages 14 and 15?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The difficulty here was that I wasn't able to take a direct line to Stotina, and because of newly-built structures. What I did to get the correct range was to move at the same distance I made a curve and tried to locate a location where I would get a sight line to the location -- to the direction of fire. The victim was shot dead and what I believe is that there were no -- she was found. The additional information is -- it was a woman on the -- on a terrace when she was hit, so that's -- led me to conclude that she would have been identifiable, the range 420 metres which wasn't that extreme.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could now turn, sir, to incident number 4, pages 15 and 16 of the hard copy, pages 16 and 17 of the e-court version. Can you tell us about this incident, please?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: In this incident an elderly male was shot in the ankle. He was shot -- well, I made a mistake, there was some -- a slight mistake as to the victim and the witness. The location of the victim marked on the sketch was actually the location of the witness, and the location of the victim was somewhere on the cemetery but was not given precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but if I could, when you say the location of the victim was somewhere on the cemetery, there are, on this sketch, two locations labelled cemetery. Can you tell us which of those two locations you're referring to when you say the victim was somewhere on the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: On the witness on the DVD, the witness points to the cemetery on the eastern side of the road. So that's the upper portion of the -- portion of the sketch. And again here you have the side picture of -- the photograph on page 16 was again taken from Stotina, and apart from being able to get a clear view of the witness, you would also have been able to get a clear view of the -- of the graveyard. Not always, of course, because there are tombstones and trees but you would be able to see people move on the graveyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, for purposes of clarification and to make sure that we all understand what you are talking about, on the photograph on page 16 or again page 17 in e-court, the arrow indicating case number 4, what does that arrow point to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The arrow points to the location of the witness instead of the victim, because there was no precise location of the victim given by the witness, apart from the graveyard, on the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again on this photograph, which of the two visible cemeteries are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I am referring to the upper part of -- the one above the road with the -- the higher wall with the red car in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Lieutenant van der Weijden, in light of the instructions that were given to you, what conclusions did you draw with respect to incident number 4?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The conclusion would be that it would be very difficult, because of all the tombstones and the trees from the eastern side -- from the eastern side of the cemetery, or just around him to get a clean shot of -- a clean sight picture of the victim. And in that, unless he would have been intentionally shot in the ankle at that short range, which I think is -- is unlikely. But the picture represents the view from Stotina from the same location as the previous incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, in order to in effect cluster the incidents based on the alleged shooting location, I would now ask you to skip ahead, please, to incident number 9, which is on pages 27 and 28 of the hard copy or pages 28 and 29 of P 09808 in e-court. Lieutenant van der Weijden, can you please tell us what steps you took to produce the report concerning incident number 9?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Again, the exact location of the victim was determined with the use of the DVD, and also pointed out by the investigator with the use of a GPS. On the location of the victim I tried to determine what possibilities there were for the shooter to take a position. The origin of the -- the direction the victims came from would -- would have been ruled out. Because it is completely blocked by structures, there is no way to get a view on the victims unless from an extremely close range that would be under 25 metres. The rear, to the north, would be covered by the -- the buildings as well, along with the small alleyway to their east. That only leaves the alley and towards the south. And if we look at the picture on the second -- on page 28, from Stotina, in these cases, in urban scenarios, streets often create a sort of a tunnel, which points back to the victim, which points back to the -- to the shooter location. And from the location of the victim, the only houses you could see which would offer a shooting position were -- was the house in Stotina. So they look straight down into the alleyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, this incident, sir, offers an opportunity for me to ask you questions about the amount of time that the victim would have been visible to the shooter and what effect that would have on the shooter's ability to distinguish the target and/or to take a shot at the target. Can you comment on that based on the photograph contained on page 28 or page 29 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, it would be very difficult in a short amount of time. The victims -- what they might have been doing is first peeking around the corner and then walking across. They would only be visible for a couple of seconds. It would be sort of shady conditions, so it would be very difficult for the shooter to identify the people -- the victims. The only thing that is different in this is that there are boys. In the picture there is visible the windowsills of the house with the satellite disk, the satellite disk, and in that same sight picture were the victims so you would be able to quickly compare them, it would still take time during which time they could have already have crossed, so it would be difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about if the location at Stotina were to be considered a static location, would that have any impact on the answer that you just gave us?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would still -- it would give the shooter more time -- of -- it would take the shooter less time to calculate the distance and compensate, scope for the distance. But it still would be -- would be difficult to identify the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about, sir, in a situation, in a hypothetical situation, perhaps, where a number of individuals passed in front of this spot over a given course of time? How would that impact, if at all, upon the shooter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, if shooting like this and are -- shooting ranges like this where I have fired myself where you look down alleys, it's very difficult because the human eye is -- especially in a side picture like this there are lots of roofs and if you look down at the roofs, the thing that stands most -- stands out most is movement. So first if there was a group of people, the first you would be alerted to would just walk across. You would be alerted, and then with more people walking that way, you would probably only be able to fire at the third or fourth person identifying -- after having identified them. So it -- it takes time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Lieutenant van der Weijden, in -- again in light of the instructions that you were provided, can you reach any conclusions with respect to incident 9?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's very difficult after that time to be completely 100 per cent sure, but the -- almost the only option that there was from that location which offers a shooting position would be the house on Stotina, the upper levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, if you would now turn to incident 10, which is reflected on pages 29 and 30 of the report, or pages 30 and 31 in the e-court version of P 08908 and I would ask you, sir, what exact steps you took to produce this part of your report.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Here again it's -- I visited the exact incident site, made a rough sketch. From there I tried to determine what possibilities there were, possibilities there were. 180 degrees is blocked by the house east of the victim, which I have made -- which I coloured grey. The action of the victim, what he was doing, he was walk towards the water and back to get water and walking back up. If the shooter would have been on the other side of the -- of the river the victim was almost out -- out of sight for the shooter if he had been on the other side of the bank. Which would make it very difficult -- very -- not very obvious for the shooter to be on the other side of the banks, of the river. Again, looking in the direction that the arrow is pointed, so roughly 186 degrees, that again points to the house in Stotina as being the most suitable shooting location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me ask you just a hypothetical question. This route that you've drawn of the victim relatively -- relatively straight line from the river to the house, if that route of the victim had been rather a different route and he had gone between the two flower beds, as you've drawn them, what effect, if any, would that have upon the information contained in this part of your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It give -- it would give the shooter more time to take -- take aim of -- judge the distance, compensate, and take the shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Lieutenant van der Weijden, let me ask you now sir to turn to page 30. There are several photographs. Photo A, can you tell us what photo A on page 30 or page 31 in e-court represents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Photo A is the exact location -- is taken from the exact location of the incident towards Stotina, and with -- within the picture I blew up the house to a bigger size to identify the possible locations which were the breaked-up windows, which I was told that -- that weren't present at that time. And the second photo, photo B is just a reverse side picture taken from Stotina two metres in front of the house towards the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, based on the instructions that you were given, what conclusions did you reach with respect to incident 10?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That the most suitable location would be Stotina. And that the range -- through the range, 450 metres, would be adequate enough to identify the victim -- the victim as combatant or non-combatant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could turn sir to incident 13 which is on page 34 and -- 34 through 36 of the report and those would be pages 35 through 37 of the e-court version. Can you tell us, Lieutenant van der Weijden, what steps you took to produce this part of your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Again, visiting the location, this again was blocked by new buildings by moving up the -- the apartment building above the same -- right above the incident site on the floor one -- one below the upper level, from there I took the picture that I -- that shows the house in Stotina. With this incident, because the apartment building is U-shaped, that limits -- that just points back to a certain direction where the shot must have originated from. Again, that possibility of pointing back to the house in Stotina. As for the victims -- of himself, he was an eight-year-old boy. At the entrance there was a doorway. An eight-year-old boy reaches up about halfway the door, so would be readily identifiable as a child and he was playing, so he had been -- he would have been visible for a longer time. On the alleged shooting position, which is the ridge of Mount Hum, which was 800 metres away, I don't agree with that because that position would have been out in the open and given the time of the incident on the 2nd of February, it would be cold and if looking on the photo A above Stotina, Mount Hum was not covered by trees. So it would have been very difficult to move about during daylight unseen. The temperatures would be low, so it would be -- yeah, not likely that someone would be outside, out in the open, take a shot there and stay there. So for me, the conclusion was that the house in Stotina, which offers protection from the elements, would be a far more likely option.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what was the distance, if you were able to calculate it, from the house in Stotina to the location of the victim?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The house in Stotina was 533 metres so that's nearby -- it's still a considerable -- considerable distance for -- but compared to the ridge at 800 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. It was, of course, our intention to go through all 12 of the incidents. We have been able to go through seven of them. We would respectfully request the opportunity to go through the remaining five incidents first thing tomorrow. In the event we are not able to do that due to time constraints, so be it, but we would ask the same series of questions with respect to the remaining five incidents which we have asked with respect to the first seven. So we are entirely in the Trial Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. The mastery that you used to get through what we have seen today, and there are five remaining cases which will perhaps take you 15 to 20 minutes. So that will give the Defence the four hours to cross-examine. The Judges will do their best not to ask any questions to allow the Prosecution to finish, and then Defence to cross-examine. As it's 7.00, we adjourn until tomorrow, 2.15, and we will have to finish by 7.00 tomorrow. So until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
